subject: general
question:
**Select the correct option for the Direct Speech conversion of the sentence below. **

He observed that, had market liquidity vanished entirely, the exchange would have suspended trading.

options.text: He said, "If market liquidity vanishes entirely, the exchange suspends trading."
He said, "Had market liquidity vanished entirely, the exchange would have suspended trading."
He said, "The exchange will suspend trading if market liquidity had vanished entirely."
He said, "If the exchange suspended trading, it was because market liquidity vanished entirely."

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. He said, "Had market liquidity vanished entirely, the exchange would have suspended trading.".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence provided is in reported speech and refers to a hypothetical situation in the past.
 
• It uses the conditional structure **"Had + past participle, would have + past participle"**, which is typical of the third conditional.
 
• Option 2 retains the correct meaning and tense of the original sentence while converting it into direct speech.

Correct sentence: *He said, "Had market liquidity vanished entirely, the exchange would have suspended trading."*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1st Conditional Sentence:**

 
 
• **Structure:** If + Present Simple, will + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If it rains, we will cancel the picnic.
 
• **Usage:** Describes real or possible situations in the future with likely outcomes.
 
 
 
• **2nd Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure:** If + Past Simple, would + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If I were rich, I would travel the world.
 
• **Usage:** Refers to unreal or hypothetical situations in the present or future.
 
 
 
• **3rd Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure:** If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle.
 
• **Example:** If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
 
• **Usage:** Refers to unreal past situations and their imagined outcomes.
